subject.title: Bug: OpenClaw 2026.4.9 exposes agent internal thinking (English) to user

question: Should maintainers fix this issue as a narrow embedded-streaming security bug now, or explicitly consolidate it into a broader reasoning-leakage fix path?
rationale: The source-level gap can expose hidden reasoning to chat recipients, but the issue is security-sensitive and already carries no-new-fix-pr plus needs-security-review labels, so automation should not start a new repair without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fix the streaming scanner now
options.body: Align THINKING_TAG_SCAN_RE and related open/close helpers with the shared sanitizer grammar and add focused stream tests for attribute-bearing tags.

options.title: Consolidate under broader leakage work
options.body: Keep this issue open but route the exact scanner gap into a named canonical reasoning-leakage issue before closing any duplicates.

options.title: Defer pending live proof
options.body: Require a fresh WeChat or channel-level live reproduction before changing the security-sensitive delivery path.

recommendation.title: Fix the streaming scanner now
recommendation.body: Align THINKING_TAG_SCAN_RE and related open/close helpers with the shared sanitizer grammar and add focused stream tests for attribute-bearing tags.

likelyOwner.reason: The current routing decision spans security-sensitive delivery behavior and shared sanitizer ownership, and steipete has the strongest maintainer-history signal in the shared reasoning-tag contract.
